intro: Ordering 25, 50 or 100 blank t-shirts for an event, a club or a merchandise drop is where the model, the retailer and the size split all start to matter. This guide gives you the per-piece maths for Fruit of the Loom in Europe, an honest look at wholesale prices, and a step-by-step ordering checklist that avoids the usual mistakes.

body_html:
Which t-shirt should you buy in bulk for printing?

For events, merchandise, clubs and campaigns the choice comes down to two Fruit of the Loom models, with a third for special cases:

  • Valueweight T (61-036), approx. 165 g/m² — the default. 100 % cotton, tubular body without side seams, a smooth surface for screen printing and DTG, and the widest colour range. If you are not sure, order this.
  • Original T (61-082), approx. 145 g/m² — lighter and slightly cheaper at wholesale. Fine for one-day events, summer festivals and giveaways where the tee will be worn a handful of times.
  • Heavy Cotton T (61-212), approx. 195 g/m² — thicker, boxier, more durable. Choose it for staff tees or merchandise people will wear for years.

Whatever you choose, keep the whole order on one model: sizing, colour shade and print behaviour then stay identical across the run, and reorders match. Our {{LINK:t-shirts|t-shirt model guide}} has the full breakdown.

How do wholesale prices compare?

German textile wholesalers list Fruit of the Loom tees from approx. €2.24–2.61 per piece (checked September 2026). That is a genuinely lower number, but the conditions matter for a bulk buyer:

  • textil-grosshandel.eu quotes prices excluding VAT and states that it sells exclusively to commercial customers.
  • textilwaren24.eu includes VAT but ships only within Germany (€5.95) and Austria (€13.95).
  • "From" prices usually apply to the cheapest colour and size; coloured tees cost more.

If you are a registered business in Germany ordering 200 white tees, the wholesaler wins. If you are a club in Ireland, a start-up in the Netherlands or a school in Spain ordering 30 navy tees, the wholesale route is often closed or expensive once VAT and cross-border shipping are added — and Marmalade Co.'s price guarantee (identical product found cheaper is matched) covers the gap for products you can genuinely buy elsewhere. The full picture is in our {{LINK:cheapest|European price comparison}}.

How to split sizes for a group order

The most common bulk mistake is not the model or the shop but the size split. For a mixed adult group with no size list, a typical distribution is roughly 10 % S, 25 % M, 30 % L, 20 % XL, 10 % 2XL and 5 % 3XL — adjust for your audience (student groups skew smaller, trade teams larger). If you can collect sizes, use chest measurements: S 89–94 cm, M 95–100, L 101–106, XL 107–112, 2XL 113–118, 3XL 119–124. Kids' tees run by height: 104, 116, 128, 140, 152, 164.

Step by step: ordering bulk tees for printing

  1. Fix the design and colour count. One or two ink colours keep screen-printing set-up cheap; full-colour artwork points to DTG for runs under about 25 pieces.
  2. Choose the garment colour. Light colours are cheapest to print (no white underbase). Solid colours are more predictable than heathers, which contain polyester.
  3. Get two printer quotes with your quantity and colour count before ordering blanks, so the blank order matches what the printer needs.
  4. Order blanks in one go from the {{SHOP:/collections/t-shirts-herre|t-shirt collection at Marmalade Co.}}. Five-plus pieces trigger the 10 % discount; one parcel means one €7 fee. Dispatch is within 0–1 business day and delivery 2–3 business days.
  5. Check the delivery for sizes and colours before handing over to the printer; blanks are easy to exchange, printed tees are not.
  6. Keep a few spares blank for latecomers and misprints.

Which technique fits your run — screen print, DTG, vinyl or embroidery — is covered in our {{LINK:printing|printing guide}}.

Timing: how long does a bulk order take?

Blanks are the fast part: 2–3 business days from Marmalade Co. Printing is the slow part — expect one to two weeks for a standard screen-printing job and longer in September–November when schools, clubs and companies all order at once. Work backwards from your event date, add a week of buffer, and order blanks as soon as the size list is final.

faq.q: What is the cheapest blank t-shirt for bulk printing?
faq.a: Among branded blanks, the Fruit of the Loom Valueweight T (approx. 165 g/m²) and the lighter Original T (approx. 145 g/m²) are the cheapest widely available options. At Marmalade Co. they cost €6.26 each from 5 pieces incl. VAT with a €7 flat DHL fee; German wholesalers list from-prices around €2.24–2.61 but excluding VAT, for business customers or with delivery limited to Germany and Austria.

faq.q: How much do 50 blank t-shirts cost?
faq.a: At Marmalade Co. 50 Fruit of the Loom tees cost approx. €312.75 with the automatic 10 % quantity discount (€6.26 each), plus €7 DHL shipping — approx. €319.75 delivered, or €6.40 per tee, VAT included, in mixed sizes and colours. Printing is extra and depends on the technique and number of ink colours; get two local quotes.

faq.q: Is there a minimum order for bulk t-shirts?
faq.a: Not at consumer-friendly retailers. Marmalade Co. sells from one piece and applies 5 % off at 3 pieces and 10 % off at 5 or more of the same product, so 'bulk' pricing starts at five tees. Wholesalers often require a business account rather than a minimum quantity. Screen printers, by contrast, usually quote from around 10–25 pieces because of set-up costs.

faq.q: Which sizes should I order for a group without a size list?
faq.a: A common adult split is about 10 % S, 25 % M, 30 % L, 20 % XL, 10 % 2XL and 5 % 3XL, adjusted for your group. Fruit of the Loom adult sizes by chest are S 89–94 cm, M 95–100, L 101–106, XL 107–112, 2XL 113–118 and 3XL 119–124; kids' tees run by height from 104 to 164. Always add two or three spares in M and L.

faq.q: How fast can I get bulk blanks delivered in Europe?
faq.a: Marmalade Co. dispatches within 0–1 business day and DHL delivers in an estimated 2–3 business days to Austria, Belgium, Finland, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, the Netherlands, Poland, Portugal and Spain, with tracking by e-mail. Printing typically adds one to two weeks, more in the autumn peak, so order blanks as soon as the size list is final.

faq.q: Should I order Valueweight T or Heavy Cotton T for merchandise?
faq.a: Choose Valueweight T (approx. 165 g/m²) for events, campaigns and most merch: it is cheaper, prints cleanly and is comfortable in warm weather. Choose Heavy Cotton T (approx. 195 g/m²) when the tee will be worn regularly for years, such as staff tees or premium merchandise, and you want a thicker, more structured feel.
